look_here_first: Start with sessile leaves and a 3–8 cm axillary inflorescence. The strongest split from A. simulans is that A. aphoroides inflorescences are unisexual; then confirm with 10 stamens and a relatively large 7–9 mm woolly capsule.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: limestone-derived Edwards Plateau grassland/open oak-juniper habitat

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: small unisexual flowers in axillary racemes

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: proximal pistillate and distal staminate flowers

key_traits.label: Staminate flower
key_traits.text: Sepals 4–5.5 mm; petals 3.3–4 mm, free from androphore; 10 stamens; 0 staminodes

key_traits.label: Pistillate flower
key_traits.text: Sepals 6–7 mm; styles 1.5–3 mm, tomentose; stigmas flattened

key_traits.label: Fruit seed
key_traits.text: Capsules 7–9 mm, tomentose to lanulose; seeds 3.7–5 mm, smooth to lightly tuberculate or striate

lookalikes.differences: Separate from A. humilis and A. simulans with inflorescence, flower, capsule, and seed characters; habit and habitat alone are not secure.
